A multitude of articulated claws dig deep under root and soil as the korrask waits unseen beneath colossal Wealdwoods trees. Tunneling 
beneath tree roots is nearly impossible for most creatures, yet this great centipede is able to dig itself a burrow with shovel-like claws 
easily with its prodigious strength. When near the surface of well trod game trails, it pulls back its primary mandibles, tendons 
stretched taut, and its secondary jaws pull in detritus to cover its awaiting maw. With sensitive antennae questing out on the earth, 
the insect awaits the slightest vibrations of an incoming creature. As the unfortunate creature steps between the mandibles, they erupt 
from the earth violently with a fraction of a second, slicing the prey in half, before it pulls the grisly remains into its tooth-lined gullet.

Lurker Th e korrask has Advantage on the fi rst attack roll against 
any creature it has Surprised.
Tunneler Th e korrask can burrow through solid rock at half its 
Burrow Speed and leaves a 10 ft. diameter tunnel in its wake.
Multiattack Th e korrask makes three attacks with its Bladed 
Mandibles, Flail, Ground Eruption in any combination.
Bladed Mandibles Melee Attack Roll: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one 
target. Hit: 22 (4d8 + 4) Slashing damage. If the target is a Large 
or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 13), 
and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends.
Flail Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 16, each creature in a 15 ft. Emanation 
centered on the korrask. Failure: 11 (2d6 +4) Bludgeoning damage 
and has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage.

Devour Strength Saving Th row: DC 16, each creature in a 15 ft.

Medium or smaller, it is swallowed. A swallowed creature has 
the Blinded and Restrained Conditions, has Total Cover against

Acid damage at the start of each of the korrask’s turns. If the 
korrask takes 24 damage or more on a single turn from a creature 
inside it, the korrask must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution 
Saving Th row at the end of that turn or burrow to the surface 
and regurgitate all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in 
a space within 5 ft. of the korrask, has the Prone condition. If 
the korrask dies, any swallowed creatures no longer have the 
Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 5 
ft. of movement, exiting Prone. Th e korrask can swallow up to 
three Medium creatures or six Small creatures at a time.
Multitude of Claws Trigger: A creature hits it with a melee attack. 
Response - Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 16, the triggering creature.
Failure: 11 (2d6+4) Slashing damage as the korrask lashes out.
Senses Blindsight 20 ft., Tremorsense 35 ft., Passive Perception 13
Challenge 7 (XP 2,900; PB 3)
Defensive Instinct (1/Day) Battered and hurt, the giant centipede 
pushes itself deeper into the earth to avoid further bloodshed.
Reaction - Trigger: When the korrask is Bloodied. Response - 
Constitution Saving Th row: DC 16, the korrask. Success: Th e korrask 
gains +2 bonus to its Armor Class (total AC 21) for the duration of 
the combat encounter.
Skills Perception +1, Stealth +2
Encountering Th e mind of the korrask understands little 
besides the primal patience of awaiting prey and the eruption 
of violence once one is caught. With practice, a Traveler can 
spot the telltale mandibles rising from the soil, and if fortunate 
enough, can lure the creature out by tossing live bait or a heavy 
sack of meat onto mound of earth between the mandibles.
Resistances Bludgeoning, Lightning, Poison
Immunities Blinded, Prone
With often only one opportunity to strike, the 
scything talons are razor sharp to easily cut 
through both bone and any intervening roots 
The dim light of the Wealdwoods glint 
off two oddly sharp stones. Often the 
only sign of an awaiting korrask before 
the lethal strike
Petal-like muscles cascade down the center of the 
arthropod, helping pull down earth and stone, as 
well as sifting through organic componds to digest 
during long intervals while awaiting prey
